claim: ATP acts as universal cellular energy cofactor fuelling all life processes, including gene expression, metabolism, and transport.
source: ATP acts as universal cellular energy cofactor fuelling all life processes, including gene expression, metabolism, and transport.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about ATP's role in cells.

claim: Arabidopsis sensor lines expressing ATeam1.03-nD/nA in the cytosol were generated.
source: Here, we establish MgATP2- measurement in living plants using the fluorescent protein biosensor ATeam1.03-nD/nA. We generate Arabidopsis sensor lines and investigate the sensor in vitro under conditions appropriate for the plant cytosol.
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation of transgenic Arabidopsis lines expressing the sensor.

claim: The sensor responds rapidly and reliably to MgATP2- changes in planta.
source: We establish an assay for ATP fluxes in isolated mitochondria, and demonstrate that the sensor responds rapidly and reliably to MgATP2- changes in planta.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing sensor responses to MgATP2- changes.

claim: Different MgATP2- concentrations exist between tissues in Arabidopsis seedlings.
source: A MgATP2- map of the Arabidopsis seedling highlights different MgATP2- concentrations between tissues and within individual cell types, such as root hairs.
evidence: The manuscript presents imaging data showing tissue-specific differences in MgATP2- levels.

claim: Different MgATP2- concentrations exist within individual cell types, such as root hairs.
source: A MgATP2- map of the Arabidopsis seedling highlights different MgATP2- concentrations between tissues and within individual cell types, such as root hairs.
evidence: The manuscript presents imaging data showing cell-to-cell variation in root hairs.

claim: Progression of hypoxia reveals substantial plasticity of ATP homeostasis in seedlings.
source: Progression of hypoxia reveals substantial plasticity of ATP homeostasis in seedlings, demonstrating that ATP dynamics can be monitored in the living plant.
evidence: The manuscript presents time-course data of ATP levels during hypoxia treatment.

claim: ATP is used as a metabolic building block.
source: It is used as a metabolic building block and as a cofactor to couple exergonic and endergonic reactions, making ATP as fundamental to life as proton gradients and the genetic code.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about ATP function.

claim: ATP acts as a cofactor to couple exergonic and endergonic reactions.
source: It is used as a metabolic building block and as a cofactor to couple exergonic and endergonic reactions, making ATP as fundamental to life as proton gradients and the genetic code.
evidence: This is established biochemical knowledge about ATP function.

claim: De-phosphorylation to ADP and AMP, and re-phosphorylation to ATP allow high energy fluxes based on relatively small pool sizes in the cell.
source: De-phosphorylation to ADP and AMP, and re-phosphorylation to ATP allow high energy fluxes based on relatively small pool sizes in the cell (Rich, 2003).

claim: The major sites of ATP synthesis are ATP synthases driven by the proton motive force established across the inner membrane of the mitochondria.
source: The major sites of ATP synthesis are ATP synthases driven by the proton motive force established across the inner membrane of the mitochondria, and the plastid thylakoids in plants.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cellular bioenergetics.

claim: The major sites of ATP synthesis include plastid thylakoids in plants.
source: The major sites of ATP synthesis are ATP synthases driven by the proton motive force established across the inner membrane of the mitochondria, and the plastid thylakoids in plants.
evidence: This is established knowledge about plant cellular bioenergetics.

claim: Plastids consume substantial amounts of ATP in the Calvin-Benson cycle.
source: The ATP produced typically fuels the wide range of energy-demanding processes, such as motility, transport, and gene expression, in other parts of the cell, although plastids also consume substantial amounts of ATP in the Calvin-Benson cycle, to an extent that varies substantially with the light/dark cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about plant metabolism.

claim: ATP consumption by plastids in the Calvin-Benson cycle varies substantially with the light/dark cycle.
source: The ATP produced typically fuels the wide range of energy-demanding processes, such as motility, transport, and gene expression, in other parts of the cell, although plastids also consume substantial amounts of ATP in the Calvin-Benson cycle, to an extent that varies substantially with the light/dark cycle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about plant metabolism.

claim: Coupling of ATP production and consumption requires ATP/ADP exchange between the organelles and cytosol.
source: Coupling of these interactions requires ATP/ADP exchange between the organelles and cytosol.

claim: Regulation of cytosolic and organelle ATP levels gives rise to complex ATP dynamics in plant cells.
source: Thus, regulation of cytosolic and organelle ATP levels, and ATP/ADP transport across the mitochondrial and plastid envelope, give rise to particularly complex ATP dynamics in plant cells, that is critically dependent on the tissue type and external conditions (Neuhaus et al., 1997; Flügge, 1998; Reiser et al., 2004; Haferkamp et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: ATP dynamics in plant cells are critically dependent on the tissue type and external conditions.
source: Thus, regulation of cytosolic and organelle ATP levels, and ATP/ADP transport across the mitochondrial and plastid envelope, give rise to particularly complex ATP dynamics in plant cells, that is critically dependent on the tissue type and external conditions (Neuhaus et al., 1997; Flügge, 1998; Reiser et al., 2004; Haferkamp et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Purified ATeam1.03-nD/nA was selective for MgATP2-.
source: To interpret in vivo measurements in the Arabidopsis sensor lines, we aimed for an in-depth understanding of key sensor characteristics. The Kd(ATP), nucleotide specificity and pH sensitivity of the original ATeam family variants were characterised for use in animal cells at 37°C (Imamura et al., 2009). While the newer ATeam1.03-nD/nA variant shows an improved dynamic range (Kotera et al., 2010), its other properties have not been characterised in detail, particularly at the pH and temperature conditions likely to be experienced in the plant cytosol, mitochondrial matrix or plastid stroma. We therefore characterised purified ATeam1.03-nD/nA protein in vitro (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript presents in vitro characterization data showing sensor specificity.

claim: The sensor emission spectrum showed a well-defined ratiometric shift in response to ATP.
source: The sensor emission spectrum showed a well-defined ratiometric shift in response to ATP. The mseCFP peak (475 nm) decreased and the cp173-mVenus peak (527 nm) increased, with increasing ATP concentrations in the high micromolar/low millimolar range (Figure 2B).
evidence: The manuscript presents spectroscopic data showing sensor response to ATP.
